main_text.l: V. Habacuc, conscientia ignoratiae hominum pudefactus, erumpit in Dei laudes & θεολογίαν[?], v.1. Ac ubi supplicitèr pro populo Iudaico intercedens, precatus esset, ut Deus in ira sua misericordiae recordari uellet, v.2. magnifica Dei opera ad Auctoris laudem recenset. Memi-nit autem, 1. Νομοθέτας[?], seu promulgatae legis, & miraculorum quae tum perācta fuerunt, v.3 & 4. 2. Plagarum paulo ante eductionem Israelitarum Aegyptiis infli-ctarum, & quidem κατὰ αὐτενδοχλὼ[?], pestis mentione facta: nisi quis haec de peste, qua Cananaeos[?], tum, cum Israelitas ex Aegypto Deus educeret, exstirpare aggressus est, malitacc ipere: v.5. 3. Distributionis terrae Canaan, secundum xii. tribus Israelis, & expulsionis Gentium: v.6. 4. Defensionis Israelitarum aduersus Midianitas & alios hostes: v.7. 5. Transitus per mare rubrum, & per Iordanem fluuium: v.8. 6. Potentiae & ueracitatis Dei documentorum: v.9.10. 7. Praelij, in quo de coelo pugnauit Dominus pro Iosua & Israelitis aduersus Cananaeos, Amorrhaeos & alios populos, Sole stante:

page.notes: Running head is "PROLEGOMENA" with "Caput 3." set beneath it; I included the latter in the running head. The asterisk in the left margin beside "Trā situs" has no note text; it appears to be a reference mark only. Doubtful readings: "θεολογίαν" (the Greek is blurred), "Νομοθέτας" (accents uncertain), "κατὰ αὐτενδοχλὼ" (the rest of the Greek word is illegible), "Cananaeos" (the spelling is uncertain where the printed form is blurred, and it appears as "Cananzos" in the first instance). "malitacc ipere" is probably a printing error for "malitaccipere", left as printed. "conscientia" and "ignoratiae" are read from the long-s forms "confcientia" and "ignoratiae". The verse reference "V.11." is treated as a level 3 head, set apart below the text.
